entry: American singer, songwriter, actress, and dancer. The youngest child of the Jackson family, she achieved global stardom with the albums *Control* (1986) and *Rhythm Nation 1814* (1989), and her sound and choreography helped drive the growth of [[MTV]]. A 2004 Super Bowl halftime performance with [[Justin Timberlake]] sparked a controversy, after which her career declined. Jackson is one of the best-selling music artists of all time, with estimated sales of over 100 million records. Her accolades include five [[Grammy Awards]], 11 Billboard Music Awards, and an induction into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]].

American actress, businesswoman, and author. Known as one of the earliest scream queens, Leigh also starred in dramatic productions for [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer]]. Her role as Marion Crane in [[Alfred Hitchcock]]'s [[Psycho (1960 film)|*Psycho*]] (1960) won her a Golden Globe Award and an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress. She later starred with her daughter, [[Jamie Lee Curtis]], in *The Fog* (1980) and *Halloween H20: 20 Years Later* (1998). Leigh co-founded Curtleigh Productions with [[Tony Curtis]] and wrote four books, two of which were novels, between 1984 and 2002.

American singer-songwriter and rock performer, noted for her powerful mezzo-soprano vocals and stage presence. She rose to prominence in 1967 as lead singer of the San Francisco psychedelic rock band Big Brother and the Holding Company, then performed as a solo artist with her own backing groups. She appeared at [[Woodstock]] in 1969. Joplin died of a heroin overdose at age 27. Her cover of Kris Kristofferson's "Me and Bobby McGee" reached number one in March 1971, after her death, and her second solo album, *Pearl*, also reached number one on the Billboard 200. In 1995 she became the first female solo artist inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in her first year of eligibility. [[Rolling Stone]] ranked her number 28 on its 2008 list of the "200 Greatest Singers of All Time."

Member of the elite infantry corps and household troops of the [[Ottoman Empire]]. The corps was one of the first infantry forces equipped primarily with [[Firearm|firearms]], adopted under Murad II (r. 1421–1444, 1446–1451). Originally recruited through the devşirme system of child levy, which took mainly Christian boys from the [[Balkans]], the janissaries were forbidden to marry until retirement. By the 17th century civilians had bought their way into the corps, which lost much of its military character. Resistant to reform, the corps was abolished by [[Mahmud II]] in 1826 in the Auspicious Incident, in which 6,000 or more janissaries were executed.

Mob assault on the [[United States Capitol]] by supporters of President [[Donald Trump]], who were responding to his claims that the 2020 election had been stolen. Attackers sought to prevent Congress from counting Electoral College votes confirming the victory of [[Joe Biden]]. The FBI estimates 2,000–2,500 people entered the building. Five people died within 36 hours, and 174 police officers were injured. Academic debate continues over whether to characterize the event as an attempted coup. The House impeached Trump for incitement of insurrection, and the Senate acquitted him. On January 20, 2025, Trump granted clemency to all rioters, including those convicted of violent offenses.

Visual and material arts produced in Japan, from ancient pottery to modern [[Manga|manga]] and [[Anime|anime]]. The history of Japanese art begins with human habitation in Japan in the 10th millennium BCE. The earliest complex art was produced in the 7th and 8th centuries in connection with [[Buddhism]]. Until modern times the Japanese wrote with a brush, and painting became the preferred artistic expression. In the [[Edo period]], [[Ukiyo-e]] woodblock prints became a major form and proved instrumental in the Western world's 19th-century dialogue with Japanese art. Sculpture declined as a medium, since most large Japanese sculpture was associated with religion. Japanese lacquerware decorated with maki-e was exported to Europe and China until the 19th century. The Meiji period (1868–1912) brought an abrupt influx of Western styles.

Regional and traditional foods of Japan, known as washoku and based on rice with miso soup. Side dishes often feature fish, pickled vegetables, and vegetables cooked in broth. Seafood is commonly grilled or served raw as [[Sushi|sushi]], and deep-fried in batter as tempura. Buddhism long discouraged eating meat, but meat-based dishes such as tonkatsu became common after the modernization of the 1880s. Historically influenced by [[Chinese cuisine]], Japanese cuisine has adapted foreign dishes, including [[Ramen|ramen]], [[Curry|curry]], and hamburgers, to Japanese tastes. In 2011 Japan overtook France as the country with the most three-star Michelin restaurants, and [[Tokyo]] had the most three-star restaurants of any city as of 2018. In 2013 Japanese cuisine was added to the UNESCO Intangible Heritage List.

Body of works composed in the Japanese language, shaped by contact with Chinese and Indian literature. Early texts were often written in Classical Chinese. The earliest literary works, including [[Kojiki|*Kojiki*]] (712), date from the Nara period. During the [[Heian period]] (794–1185), literature developed its own style through the use of kana, and [[Murasaki Shikibu]] wrote [[The Tale of Genji|*The Tale of Genji*]] in the early 11th century. Later, [[Haiku|haiku]] was refined by Matsuo Bashō in the 17th century. Western literary influence grew during the Meiji era, and [[Yasunari Kawabata]] and [[Kenzaburō Ōe]] won Nobel Prizes in Literature in 1968 and 1994.

Traditional stories, folktales, and beliefs that emerged in the islands of the Japanese archipelago. [[Shinto]] traditions are its cornerstone, and its pantheon holds uncountable kami, or spirits, tied to the archipelago's topography and to agriculturally based [[Folk religion]]. Contact with Chinese and Indian myths, including [[Buddhism]], also shaped its beliefs. The two oldest surviving sources are [[Kojiki|*Kojiki*]] (712) and *Nihon Shoki* (720). They relate the origins of the islands and of the imperial family, which claims direct descent from the sun goddess [[Amaterasu]] and her grandson Ninigi. The Edo-period scholar Motoori Norinaga's commentaries on the *Kojiki* are still studied for their influence on the understanding of Japanese myths.

Marine [[Crab|crab]] species, the largest crab found in waters around Japan. Its scientific name is *Macrocheira kaempferi*. Reaching up to 3.7 m (12.1 ft) from claw to claw, it has the largest leg span of any arthropod, and its carapace can grow to 40 cm (16 in) wide. It is the sole living member of its genus. The crab is sought by fisheries and considered a delicacy in Japan, and conservation efforts aim to prevent overfishing. It camouflages itself by attaching sponges and other organisms to its shell.

Atrocities committed by the [[Empire of Japan]] across the Asia-Pacific region before and during World War II, mainly in the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]] and the [[Pacific War]]. They included massacres, sexual slavery, torture, and human experimentation, including by [[Unit 731]]. Deaths are estimated at between 19 million and 30 million. Japanese officials have issued apologies since the 1950s, but some have been criticized as insincere, and some politicians have paid respects at the Yasukuni Shrine. Some members of the [[Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|Liberal Democratic Party]] have denied some atrocities.

Mixed writing system combining logographic [[Kanji|kanji]], adopted from [[Chinese characters]], with the syllabaries [[Hiragana|hiragana]] and [[Katakana|katakana]]. Hiragana is used mainly for native words and grammatical elements, and katakana for foreign names, loanwords, and onomatopoeia. Almost all written sentences mix kanji and kana, which makes the system one of the most complicated in use. There are 2,136 commonly used kanji (*jōyō kanji*) as of 2010, and students must learn 1,026 before graduating sixth grade. Each kana syllabary has 46 basic characters, and both derive from man'yōgana, Chinese characters used for their sounds in the Nara period. Texts without kanji are rare and are mostly children's books.

Official currency of Japan, the third-most traded currency in foreign exchange markets after the [[United States dollar]] and the [[Euro|euro]]. The New Currency Act of 1871 introduced the modern system, divided decimally into 100 sen or 1,000 rin. The Bank of Japan was founded in 1882. After [[World War II]], the yen lost much of its value amid a debt crisis and hyperinflation. It was pegged to the dollar under the Bretton Woods system and has floated since February 1973. The Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Japan have intervened in the market to slow exchange rate movements, including in 1998–2003, 2010–2011, 2022, and 2024.

Opaque variety of [[Chalcedony]], a fine-grained form of [[Quartz]], usually red, yellow, brown, or green. The reddish color comes from iron inclusions. Jasper breaks with a smooth surface and can be highly polished, so it is used for vases, jewelry, seals, snuff boxes, and gemstones. Its density is typically 2.5 to 2.9 g/cm³. Jasper was a favorite gem in the ancient world, and on [[Crete|Minoan Crete]] it was carved into seals around 1800 BC. The name comes from Greek *iaspis*, meaning "spotted or speckled stone."

Yellowish or greenish discoloration of the skin and eyes caused by high levels of bilirubin. In adults it usually indicates an underlying disease, such as liver dysfunction or a blocked bile duct. It is common in babies, with an estimated 80% affected in their first week of life. Causes range from [[Hepatitis]] and [[Cirrhosis]] to [[Medication|medications]], gallstones, and [[Cancer]]. Treatment depends on the cause, and [[Surgery]] is typically required if a bile duct is blocked. Newborns may be treated with phototherapy. The word comes from French *jaunisse*, meaning "yellow disease."

High-level programming language and core technology of the Web, alongside [[HTML]] and [[CSS]]. Netscape had Brendan Eich devise the language in 1995. It first shipped as LiveScript and was renamed JavaScript for its official release that December. Ecma International's TC39 technical committee maintains it. Web browsers include a dedicated JavaScript engine that executes client code, and the most popular runtime for non-browser use is Node.js.The language has dynamic typing, prototype-based object orientation, and first-class functions, and it supports event-driven, functional, and imperative styles. Despite its similar name and syntax, it is distinct from [[Java (programming language)|Java]]. In 2025 it was the most widely used programming language on [[GitHub]].

High-level, general-purpose, memory-safe, object-oriented programming language. Java was designed by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems and released in May 1995. It is intended to let programmers write once, run anywhere, because compiled bytecode runs on any Java virtual machine (JVM). Its syntax resembles [[C (programming language)|C]] and [[C++]], but it has fewer low-level facilities. Oracle, which bought Sun in 2010, offers its own HotSpot JVM, but the official reference implementation is the open-source OpenJDK, the default JVM for almost all [[Linux]] distributions. Java was the third most popular programming language on [[GitHub]] in 2022, although its use has gradually declined as other languages using the JVM have gained popularity.

Austronesian language spoken mainly in the central and eastern parts of the island of [[Java|Java]], Indonesia. It is the native language of more than 68 million people and the largest Austronesian language by number of native speakers. Its closest relatives include Sundanese, Madurese, and [[Bali|Balinese]]. Most speakers also use Indonesian. The language has regional dialects and speech levels, from informal ngoko to formal krama, which speakers adjust to social status and context. Traditionally written in the Javanese script, an abugida derived from the Brahmic Kawi script, it has increasingly been written in the Latin alphabet since the 20th century. Javanese is co-official with Indonesian in the Special Region of Yogyakarta.

Track and field event in which a spear-like javelin is thrown as far as possible from a runway into a marked sector. It is one of the four traditional throwing events in athletics and is part of the men's [[Decathlon]] and the women's heptathlon. It originated in ancient Greece, where it was part of the pentathlon at the [[Ancient Olympic Games]] in 708 BC, and it entered the modern Olympic program for men in 1908 and for women in 1932. Athletes must not step beyond the throwing arc, and a throw is valid only if the javelin lands tip-first. The longest valid throw wins. The men's world record is 98.48 meters, set by Jan Železný in 1996, and the women's is 72.28 meters, set by Barbora Špotáková in 2008.

Spanish actor and son of actress Pilar Bardem. He won an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for playing Anton Chigurh in the [[Coen brothers]]' crime film *No Country for Old Men* (2007). He was also Oscar-nominated for *Before Night Falls* (2000), *Biutiful* (2010), and *Being the Ricardos* (2021), in which he played [[Desi Arnaz]]. He appeared in the [[James Bond]] film *Skyfall* (2012) and in [[Woody Allen]]'s *Vicky Cristina Barcelona* (2008). He married actress [[Penélope Cruz]] in 2010.

Argentine economist and politician, president of Argentina since 2023. He won election to the Chamber of Deputies in 2021 and defeated incumbent economy minister Sergio Massa in the 2023 presidential runoff. He has been described as a right-wing populist and libertarian who supports [[Laissez-faire|laissez-faire]] economics. His government has pursued spending cuts, deregulation, and monetary restraint. According to the statistics agency INDEC, inflation fell sharply and poverty declined to an estimated 31.6% in early 2025. Rising living and healthcare costs have strained public support.

Pair of articulated structures at the entrance of the [[Mouth|mouth]], used for grasping and manipulating food. In [[Vertebrate|vertebrates]], the jaw is a bony framework made up of the upper jaw, or maxilla, and the lower jaw, or mandible. The maxilla forms the central part of the facial skeleton, supports the upper teeth, and contains the maxillary sinus, the largest paranasal sinus. The mandible is the largest and strongest bone of the skull, and its condylar processes form the temporomandibular joint with the temporal bone. Muscles including the masseter, temporalis, and pterygoids drive chewing. Jaw fractures most commonly occur at the condylar neck or parasymphysis, and temporomandibular joint dysfunction affects about 5% to 12% of adults.

Indian lawyer, independence leader, and first prime minister of [[India]]. Nehru became a leader of the [[Indian National Congress]] and was designated the political heir of [[Mahatma Gandhi]]. As Congress president in 1929, he called for complete independence from the [[British Raj]]. He served as prime minister for 16 years and 286 days, from independence in 1947 until his death in office. He promoted parliamentary democracy, secularism, and science and technology, and led the establishment of the [[Non-Aligned Movement]], whose members did not join either bloc of the [[Cold War]]. Critics argue that his referral of the [[Kashmir]] dispute to the United Nations in 1948 internationalized a bilateral issue. India suffered territorial losses in the 1962 Sino-Indian War.

1975 American thriller film directed by [[Steven Spielberg]], based on the 1974 novel by Peter Benchley. It stars Roy Scheider as police chief Martin Brody, who hunts a man-eating [[Great white shark|great white shark]] that attacks beachgoers at a New England resort town. Shot mostly on location at Martha's Vineyard, Massachusetts, the production was troubled. Because the mechanical sharks often malfunctioned, Spielberg suggested the shark's presence with an ominous theme by [[John Williams]], a method compared to that of [[Alfred Hitchcock]]. The film was the highest-grossing in history until [[Star Wars (film)|*Star Wars*]] two years later, and it is regarded as the prototypical summer blockbuster. It won three Academy Awards, for editing, score, and sound. The [[Library of Congress]] selected it for the National Film Registry in 2001.

Nigerian former footballer and attacking midfielder. Okocha won 73 caps for the Nigeria national team between 1993 and 2006, scoring 14 goals, and was a member of three [[FIFA World Cup]] squads. Widely regarded as one of Africa's most talented footballers, he was known for his skill on the ball and his version of the stepover, called the Okocha stepover. He played in the [[Bundesliga]], [[Ligue 1]], and [[Premier League]], and in [[Qatar]]. Since retiring he has worked as a television pundit and in Nigerian football administration.
